title: Business license (BPOL), classification, business tangible property and machinery and tools returns, and sign permit pointers for a glass studio
question: What does a glass studio that makes and sells glass, teaches classes and maybe serves food owe the Commissioner of the Revenue in Staunton, how is it classified, and what returns are due each year?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue, City of Staunton (an elected constitutional officer who assesses and issues business licenses and assesses business property; the City Treasurer collects)
summary: Before opening, a glass studio needs a City of Staunton business license from the Commissioner of the Revenue (the city asks for the application within 30 days of starting business; state law says before). The license is $30 for estimated gross receipts up to $50,000; above that the tax is by class: retail $0.20 per $100 of gross receipts (gallery and shop sales), repair, personal and business services $0.36 (classes and commissions), contractors $0.16, wholesalers on purchases. State law requires a separate license for each business and location but lets a studio with several lines at one address elect one license at the highest applicable rate; a manufacturer selling at wholesale from the place of manufacture is exempt from license tax on that part. Attach zoning approval, any SCC registration or fictitious name certificate, the health permit if you serve food, and tell the Commissioner when you get an ABC license (a local ABC license tax is added). Renew every year by March 1 on actual receipts. Each May 1 file the business tangible personal property return listing furnaces, kilns, tools, fixtures and equipment at original cost (tax due December 5; furniture and equipment at $2.90 per $100 of assessed value, machinery and tools used in manufacturing at $1.24). Signs need a zoning sign permit (or a Certificate of Appropriateness in a historic district) and sometimes a building or electrical permit.

steps.step: Register the business name and entity, and get the state accounts
steps.who: Studio owner; State Corporation Commission; IRS; Virginia Department of Taxation
steps.how: An LLC or corporation must be registered with the State Corporation Commission and the certificate of good standing or registration goes with the license application; a sole proprietor trading under a name other than their own files a fictitious name certificate with the SCC clerk, without which the Commissioner cannot issue the license. Get an FEIN from the IRS if you will have employees (or use your Social Security number). Register with the Virginia Department of Taxation as a retail dealer to collect sales tax on glass sales. Workers' compensation coverage is required with three or more regular employees.
steps.deadline: Before the business license can be issued
steps.quote: All corporations conducting business in Virginia must be registered with the State Corporation Commission.

steps.step: Get the zoning approval (and health permit, if any) that the license application requires
steps.who: Studio owner; Planning & Zoning Division; Virginia Department of Health (if food is served)
steps.how: The city requires zoning approval for any business (see glass_studio_zoning_use); the application says a home occupation permit, where one applies, must be approved before a license is issued, and the instructions say a food service establishment must hold its health permit before applying. Attach the zoning approval or certificate of occupancy and, for a cafe, the health permit.
steps.deadline: Before applying for the business license
steps.quote: The permit must be approved before a business license can be issued.

steps.step: Work out the classification: retail, services, contractor, wholesale, or one combined license
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue (confirms the class and rate)
steps.how: Gallery and shop sales to the public are retail ($0.20 per $100). Classes, workshops, event fees and repair or custom work are repair, personal and business services ($0.36). Installation of architectural glass on others' property is contracting ($0.16, with a state contractor license). Sales to shops or galleries for resale are wholesale, taxed on purchases, and state law bars a license tax on a manufacturer for selling its own goods at wholesale from the place of manufacture. State law requires a separate license for each business and each place of business but lets a studio with several lines at one address elect one license if each line is licensable there and all are taxed at the same rate or the licensee accepts the highest rate (for a studio that sells and teaches, $0.36 on everything, or two licenses with receipts split). If the fit is unclear, call the office or ask the Commissioner in writing for a ruling on your situation, which state law allows.
steps.quote: If you are unsure of the classification of your business, please call the Commissioner of the Revenue to determine both the business classification and rate.

steps.step: Estimate the first year's gross receipts and submit the Business License Application
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue (City Hall, 1st floor)
steps.how: Fill in the Business License Application: trade and legal names, location, business type, SSN or FEIN, sales tax number, any contractor or DPOR license number, a description of the business, its classification, your estimate of gross receipts from opening day to December 31 and the tax due. Up to $50,000 the license is $30; above that multiply by the class rate. Sign it, attach the documents from steps 1 and 2 and mail it to P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402, fax it to 540-851-4022 or email it to revenue@ci.staunton.va.us. The city asks for the application within 30 days of starting business; state law says before you begin. No license issues while you owe the city delinquent business license or personal property taxes.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of beginning business (city); before beginning business (Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a))
steps.fee: $30 for gross receipts of $0-$50,000; above that, the class rate per $100 of gross receipts

steps.step: Pay the license fee or tax
steps.how: Pay with the application: by check payable to the City of Staunton, at the Treasurer's office (City Hall, 1st floor; cash, check or card, with a card fee), by mail to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 474, in the green drop box on Central Avenue under the clock tower, or online through the city's self-service portal once the Commissioner links your web account to the license account.
steps.fee: As calculated on the application; card payments carry a fee

steps.step: If you get an ABC license, tell the Commissioner; a local ABC license tax is added
steps.who: Studio owner; Virginia ABC; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: When Virginia ABC issues the license (glass_studio_food_and_events), notify the Commissioner. The city adds a local ABC license tax to the business license, prorated monthly; the 2026 renewal form lists charges from $40 to $500 by license type (for example beer and wine off premises $150), and state law caps the local tax for a wine and beer on-and-off-premises license at a restaurant in a city at $150 and for a mixed beverage restaurant license up to 100 seats at $200.
steps.deadline: When the ABC license is obtained
steps.fee: Local ABC license tax by license type, prorated monthly
steps.quote: Businesses must notify the Commissioner of the Revenue when an ABC license is obtained.

steps.step: Renew every year by March 1 and true up the first year
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: The license runs by calendar year. The Commissioner mails a renewal form; report last year's actual gross receipts by class and an estimate for the new year, apply the rate and pay. The renewal and payment must be submitted or postmarked by March 1; a late filing draws a 10% penalty and 10% a year interest. At the first renewal the actual first-year receipts replace the estimate, with a bill or credit for the difference.
steps.fee: Per the class rates; 10% late penalty
steps.quote: The renewal and payment must be submitted and/or postmarked by March 1, 2026.

steps.step: File the business tangible personal property return by May 1 (furnaces, kilns, tools, fixtures)
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: Every business owning tangible property in the city on January 1 files a return by May 1 listing each item with the year acquired and original cost; the city wants a fixed-asset list including fully depreciated items. First-time filers use the Business Personal Property Form (the 2026 version is titled Initial Return of Tangible Property, due May 1, 2026, and can be mailed, faxed or emailed to revenue@ci.staunton.va.us); afterwards the office sends a prior-year asset list each March. The glass furnace, glory hole, kilns, torches, cold-working equipment, display cases, furniture and computers all belong on it. Payment is due December 5. The furniture-and-equipment rate is $2.90 per $100 of assessed value (assessed by the city's trending schedules).
steps.deadline: Return by May 1; payment by December 5
steps.fee: Tax at $2.90 per $100 of assessed value (general tangible personal property rate on the city's Taxes page)
steps.quote: A list of fixed assets itemizing all property (including all fully depreciated items) must be submitted. This annual business personal property tax return must be filed with the Commissioner of the Revenue by May 1st.

steps.step: Ask whether the furnace and tools are machinery and tools used in manufacturing (lower rate)
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: State law segregates machinery and tools used in a manufacturing or processing business as a separate class that can carry its own rate, not above the general rate; Staunton's Taxes page lists machinery and tools at $1.24 per $100 of assessed value against $2.90 for other tangible property. Whether a studio that melts and forms glass for sale is a manufacturer for this purpose, and which items (furnace, glory hole, kilns, benches, cold shop) qualify, is the Commissioner's determination; ask when you file and, if the valuation is disputed, you may ask the Commissioner in writing to consider an independent appraisal. Idle machinery (out of use for a year, or identified in writing by April 1 as to be withdrawn) is taxed as capital instead.
steps.fee: Machinery and tools at $1.24 per $100 of assessed value (city's Taxes page)
steps.quote: The rate of tax imposed by a county, city, or town on such machinery and tools shall not exceed the rate imposed upon the general class of tangible personal property.

steps.step: Collect and file the meals tax if you sell food or drink; sales tax on glass
steps.who: Studio owner; Commissioner of the Revenue (meals tax); Virginia Department of Taxation (sales tax)
steps.how: Prepared food and drinks sold at a cafe or at events carry the city's 7% meals tax, registered with the Commissioner and filed monthly by the 20th (modelled in meals_tax_filing and glass_studio_food_and_events). Glass sales carry Virginia retail sales tax, filed with the state, not the city.
steps.deadline: Meals tax returns by the 20th of the following month
steps.quote: engaged in the business of selling meals is required to register with the Commissioner of Revenue, collect the tax and file the appropriate returns.

steps.step: Signs: zoning sign permit or Certificate of Appropriateness, plus any building or electrical permit
steps.who: Studio owner or sign contractor; Planning & Zoning Division; Building Services
steps.how: Outside the historic districts apply for a sign permit from Planning & Zoning (site sketch and sign plans; ten business days; final inspection); inside them apply for a Certificate of Appropriateness for signage. The sign application warns that some signs also need a building permit or an electrical permit; City Code § 15.10.120 (read on eCode360) prices a sign building permit at $95 per sign and sign electrical work at $75. Entrance corridor sign guidelines apply on the 13 corridors. Details in glass_studio_zoning_use.
steps.fee: Sign building permit $95.00 per sign and sign electrical $75.00 where the building code applies (City Code § 15.10.120, read on eCode360)
steps.quote: Please be aware that certain signs may require a separate

caveats: City pages and PDFs are Internet Archive copies (dates in sources). The Business License Application Instructions, the 2026 renewal form and the online payment instructions were read in the earlier bpol_business_license research (verified 2026-10-11) and their quotes are carried over.

The city's rate table on the Business License & Taxes page reproduces § 5.05.170; the eCode360 text of Chapter 5.05 was not read. The $2.90 and $1.24 rates come from the Commissioner's Taxes page as read in the earlier Staunton discovery (2026-10-10), not re-read here.

Whether a glass studio is a 'manufacturer' for the wholesale exemption (§ 58.1-3703(C)(4)) and the machinery-and-tools class (§ 58.1-3507), and how the Commissioner would split receipts between retail and services, were not confirmed; the Commissioner can rule in writing.
The combined-license election under § 58.1-3703.1(A)(1) is state law; the city's pages do not mention it.
The local ABC license tax amounts on the 2026 renewal form were read in the earlier research; the form says not all ABC charges are listed.
